reasons: Pupper V3 documents the same actuator family in a working quadruped, with public hardware, deployment and simulation resources.
A low 10:1 reduction and compact 150 g class integrated actuator are a useful starting point for a small dynamic robot.
GIM3505-8 is smaller, but the larger GIM4305 has higher published output torque and a more directly relevant walking implementation to study.
One existing actuator/controller combination reduces initial integration work; cost reduction through a custom controller can be evaluated after the first joint is characterized.
tradeoffs: At twelve actuators, catalog motor mass alone is 1.8 kg. An actual very young kitten's weight and tiny dimensions are not promised.
A low gear ratio or the Pupper label does not guarantee our required loaded response, backdrivability, durability or sim-to-real performance.
Cooling inside a fur or silicone covering can reduce sustainable torque.
The exact Pupper driver hardware, connectors, firmware and supply availability must be matched; standard GDS34, GDZ34 and GDK34 are not assumed interchangeable.

next_work: Use the selected exact-variant drawing when available; include mounts, bearing support, connectors, cable bends and folding clearance in the layout.
Evaluate walking stance, sitting, crouching and reaching with the front paw, including continuous transitions and interference.
Allocate realistic masses and calculate joint demands before claiming torque margin. Preserve short light limbs; evaluate proximal placement and transmissions.

Characterize one joint's loaded response, current-to-output-torque relationship, delay, friction and temperature before hardware-wide validation; hardware operation requires a separate explicit command.
Model the chosen controller and actuator limits in physics simulation; do not reuse Pupper policies or catalog torque limits as validated cat performance.
